account: Today has felt unusually busy, but I have no firm evidence of anything secret. The builder has installed eight lanterns around the four tables in the great hall and asked me to inspect them tomorrow at 18:00, with the secretary attending. He says the purpose is to check even, comfortable lighting; that is the only confirmed purpose I know. The neighbour is curious whether others may attend. The secretary had a second appointment book, which initially concerned me, but explained it was a provisional record made before receiving the original. The original remains authoritative. Tea with the neighbour is confirmed for today and tomorrow. Our town accounts review stalled because neither the secretary nor I could find the ledger, receipts, or payment records. I checked the treasury and saw 128 emeralds, but no accounts papers; I asked the secretary to find them for 16:30. Residents reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn. That might simply be a delivery; I have not investigated. The neighbour visited the baker this morning and reports fresh bread planned for today's market, with no special occasion for the lights known to the baker. The neighbour also heard vague talk of a bridge or port change, explicitly unconfirmed. No such proposal has come before me today, and I have asked who mentioned it and what was suggested. Taken together, the lights, bread, and scheduling could suggest preparations for some gathering, but that is only speculation: I have no evidence linking them. I am finishing tea at the dockside cottage and need to return to the office for 16:30.
